    7.6 Federalism, Emergency & the Judiciary

    Seventh Schedule lists: Union (defence, railways, banking…), State (police, agriculture, land…), Concurrent (education, forests — moved by 42nd). Residuary subjects go to the Union (Art. 248). Article 356 (President's Rule) — maximum 3 years with parliamentary approval every 6 months; S.R. Bommai (1994) curbed its misuse.

    EmergencyArticleGrounds
    National352War, external aggression, armed rebellion (not "internal disturbance" — changed by the 44th Amendment, 1978); proclaimed thrice — 1962, 1971, 1975
    President's Rule356Failure of constitutional machinery in a state
    Financial360Threat to financial stability — never proclaimed

    Judiciary: integrated single system; Supreme Court (Art. 124) — original, appellate and advisory jurisdiction; judicial review (Art. 13); basic structure doctrine — Kesavananda Bharati (1973): Parliament can amend but not destroy the Constitution's basic structure. Collegium system governs appointments (evolved through the Three Judges Cases). High Courts (Art. 214); Patna High Court (established 1916) has jurisdiction over Bihar.

    7.7 Landmark Amendments (memorise as a chain)

    AmendmentYearEffect
    42nd1976"Mini-Constitution" — Preamble words, FRs curbed, DPSP primacy, Fundamental Duties added
    44th1978Undid Emergency excesses; right to property → legal right (Art. 300A); "armed rebellion"
    52nd1985Anti-defection (10th Schedule)
    61st1989Voting age 21 → 18
    73rd & 74th1992Panchayati Raj (11th Schedule) & urban local bodies (12th Schedule)
    86th2002Right to Education (Art. 21A), 6–14 years
    101st2016GST
    103rd2019EWS reservation (10%)
    106th2023Women's reservation (Nari Shakti Vandan) — 1/3 seats, effective after delimitation

    7.8 Bihar's Polity — the Numbers BPSC Asks

    • Bihar is bicameral: Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) — 243 seats; Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) — 75 seats.
    • Lok Sabha seats from Bihar: 40; Rajya Sabha: 16.
    • First Chief Minister: Sri Krishna Singh (1946); first Governor: Jairamdas Daulatram. Patna High Court (1916) is among India's oldest.
    • Panchayati Raj in Bihar: three tiers — Gram Panchayat → Panchayat Samiti (block) → Zila Parishad; Bihar was a pioneer in 50% reservation for women in panchayats (2006) — a widely-copied model.

    Quick revision hooks: 9 Dec 1946 first meeting · 26 Nov 1949 adopted · 26 Jan 1950 in force · Art. 32 "heart and soul" · Kesavananda 1973 basic structure · 42nd mini-constitution · 44th undid Emergency · 73rd Panchayati Raj · Bihar: 243 Assembly, 75 Council, 40 Lok Sabha, 16 Rajya Sabha.

    8. Indian Economy & Bihar Economy

    Circular flow of income — the four-sector loop

    Redraw this from memory — every label is a potential one-mark answer.

    Unemployment — four types to quote

    Redraw this from memory — every label is a potential one-mark answer.

    Core concepts BPSC keeps testing

    Economics in BPSC prelims is less about theory and more about institutions, numbers, and flagship schemes. Master five anchors: growth/inflation indicators, Fiscal system, monetary policy (RBI), financial inclusion & banking structure, and Bihar's own economic profile.

    National income & growth

    GDP = Gross Domestic Product: total value of final goods and services produced within a country in a year. India measures it via the base year 2011–12 (trap: don't write 2004–05 — that was the old series). The Central Statistics Office (CSO), now under the revamped Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), releases the estimates. Key related terms: GVA (Gross Value Added) — GDP minus taxes on products plus subsidies; nominal GDP vs real GDP (real = inflation-adjusted). Economic growth rate for 2025–26 is projected around 6.3–6.8% (Economic Survey figure ~6.8% real GDP growth for FY26 — treat projections as approximate). Sectors: agriculture (~15% of GDP, employs ~42–45% of workforce), industry (~26%), services (~55%). Trap: India is a services-led economy by output but an agriculture-dependent one by employment.

    Inflation & monetary policy

    RBI's inflation target under the flexible inflation targeting framework: 4% CPI with ±2% band (2–6%), set by the government under the RBI Act (2016 amendment). The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) has 6 members (3 RBI — Governor as chair + 2; 3 external appointed by government), meets at least 4 times a year, decides repo rate by majority with the Governor's casting vote. Repo rate = rate at which RBI lends to commercial banks against securities; reverse repo = opposite. CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio) and SLR (Statutory Liquidity Ratio) are quantitative tools. Shaktikanta Das was replaced as RBI Governor by Sanjay Malhotra in December 2024 — a recent-changes trap. Money supply: M1 (narrow — currency + demand deposits), M3 (broad — includes time deposits). UPI is run by NPCI, not RBI directly.

    Budget, fiscal system & tax

    The Union Budget is presented by the Finance Minister on 1 February (since 2017; earlier last day of February — P. Chidambaram tradition broken by Arun Jaitley in Budget 2017–18). Article 112: the "Annual Financial Statement" — the word budget doesn't appear in the Constitution (classic trap). Revenue receipts vs capital receipts; fiscal deficit = total expenditure minus (revenue receipts + non-debt capital receipts). FRBM Act 2003 targets fiscal deficit ~3% of GDP. GST (launched 1 July 2017, 101st Amendment): four slabs 5/12/18/28% (plus cesses); Article 246A; GST Council chaired by the Union Finance Minister with state FMs. GST is a destination-based consumption tax. Direct taxes: administered by CBDT; indirect by CBIC.

    Banking & financial inclusion

    Nationalisation: 14 banks (19 July 1969) + 6 more (1980). RBI established 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act 1934, nationalised 1949; HQ Mumbai. SBI formed 1955 from the Imperial Bank. Regional Rural Banks: 1975 (Narasimham Committee, M. Narasimham 1975). Key inclusion schemes: PM Jan Dhan Yojana (2014) — zero-balance accounts with RuPay card and ₹2 lakh accident insurance; MUDRA (2015) — Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishore (₹50,001–₹5 lakh), Tarun (₹5–10 lakh); PM Vishwakarma (2023) for traditional artisans (18 trades); Stand-Up India — bank loans for SC/ST and women entrepreneurs. SEBI (1988, statutory 1992) regulates capital markets; IRDAI insurance; PFRDA pensions.

    Poverty, unemployment, schemes

    Poverty estimation: Tendulkar Committee methodology (used for 2009–12); Rangarajan Committee (higher lines: ₹47/day urban, ₹32/day rural — roughly); earlier Lakdawala (1993). Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) by UNDP–OPHI: dimensions health, education, living standards. Unemployment: measured by PLFS (Periodic Labour Force Survey); usual-status (ps+ss) vs current weekly status. Flagship anti-poverty/livelihood schemes: MGNREGA (2005, launched 2006) — 100 days guaranteed wage employment per rural household per year; PM Awas Yojana (2015) — rural & urban housing; PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana — 5 kg free grain; PM Kisan Samman Nidhi (2019) — ₹6,000/year in three ₹2,000 instalments to landholding farmers; PM Jan Arogya / Ayushman Bharat (2018) — ₹5 lakh annual hospitalisation cover per family (expanded to all senior citizens 70+ in 2024).

    Bihar economy — the Bihar lens

    Bihar's economy is agrarian: agriculture contributes roughly 20–22% of state GSDP but employs over half the workforce. Main crops: paddy, wheat, maize, pulses, sugarcane, potato; Bihar is India's leading producer of litchi, makhana (fox nut — Geographical Indication tag, Mithila makhana), and a major maize producer. Industry is thin — mostly agro-processing, sugar mills, and the growing IT/ITeS footprint around Patna. Per capita income is among India's lowest (roughly ₹60,000–70,000 per annum vs national ~₹2 lakh+ — figures move yearly; treat as approximate). Bihar's GSDP growth has often outpaced the national average in recent years (often reported ~9–10% nominal), driven by construction and services — a favourite BPSC question pattern.

    Bihar Economic Survey: released before the state budget (Budget for 2026–27 presented in February 2026 session — keep year-specific numbers approximate). Key Bihar institutions/schemes: Bihar Industrial Investment Promotion Policy (BIIPP); Mukhyamantri Udyami Yojana — up to ₹10 lakh support for entrepreneurs (₹5 lakh interest-free loan + ₹5 lakh subsidy); Saat Nischay (Seven Resolves) — the flagship development package (nal ka jal, pucca gali-nali, electricity, youth employment, etc.); Mukhyamantri Kanya Utthan Yojana for girl children; Bihar Student Credit Card Yojana — education loans up to ₹4 lakh; Har Ghar Nal ka Jal (tap water to every household). NITI Aayog SDG India Index — Bihar typically ranks near the bottom; BPSC asks this. JEEViKA (Bihar Rural Livelihoods Promotion Society) — the state's women's SHG movement, one of India's largest.

    High-yield traps

    • "Budget" is not a constitutional word — Article 112 says Annual Financial Statement.
    • RBI nationalised in 1949, not 1935.
    • MGNREGA = 100 days per household, not per person.
    • GST is destination-based; the 101st Amendment created Articles 246A/269A/279A.
    • PM-KISAN = ₹6,000/year in 3 instalments, landholding farmers.
    • Mithila makhana has a GI tag; Bihar leads in litchi & makhana production.
    • Fiscal deficit ≠ revenue deficit: revenue deficit = revenue expenditure − revenue receipts (a subset measure of consumption shortfall).

    9. General Science (Physics / Chemistry / Biology)

    Photosynthesis — the leaf factory

    Redraw this from memory — every label is a potential one-mark answer.

    Physics — the repeating machinery

    Motion & force: Newton's three laws; inertia is the property of mass resisting change (law I). Momentum = mass × velocity; conservation of momentum explains recoil of guns. Friction opposes relative motion — rolling friction < sliding friction (why ball bearings work). Centripetal force points to the centre (merry-go-round); centrifugal is the pseudo-force in the rotating frame.

    Work, energy, power: in the direction of force (joule). ; . (watt); . Simple machines: lever classes — class I (see-saw, fulcrum middle), class II (wheelbarrow, load middle), class III (tweezers, effort middle).

    Gravitation: ; . Escape velocity on Earth ≈ 11.2 km/s; a satellite's orbital velocity ≈ 8 km/s. Geostationary satellites orbit at ~35,800 km altitude, period 24 h, positioned over the equator (INSAT/GSAT series). Polar satellites are low-earth orbit (500–800 km), used for remote sensing (IRS, Cartosat).

    Light: Speed c ≈ 3×10⁸ m/s. Reflection (angle of incidence = angle of reflection); refraction follows Snell's law. Total internal reflection (denser→rarer, beyond critical angle) — optical fibres, sparkling diamonds, mirages. Dispersion (prism splits white light: VIBGYOR) discovered by Newton. Blue sky & red sunset = Rayleigh scattering. Myopia corrected by concave lens, hypermetropia by convex lens. Human eye: image forms on the retina; persistence of vision ≈ 1/16 s.

    Sound: longitudinal mechanical wave — needs a medium; speed ≈ 332–343 m/s in air, fastest in solids. Hearing range: 20 Hz–20 kHz; ultrasonic > 20 kHz (bats, SONAR); infrasonic < 20 Hz. SONAR = Sound Navigation and Ranging. Loudness in decibels (dB); pitch depends on frequency.

    Electricity & magnetism: Ohm's law V = IR. Superconductors have zero resistance below critical temperature. India's domestic supply: 220 V, 50 Hz AC. Fuse wire: low-melting-point alloy (lead-tin). Transformer works on mutual induction (AC only); laminated cores minimise eddy currents. Motor = electrical → mechanical (Fleming's left-hand rule); generator reverses it (right-hand rule). Lightning conductor: grounded copper rod.

    Chemistry — structure and reactions

    Atoms: Dalton's atomic theory; J.J. Thomson (electron, 1897), Rutherford (nucleus, gold-foil), Bohr (orbits), Chadwick (neutron, 1932). Atomic number = protons; mass number = protons + neutrons; isotopes = same Z, different neutrons (protium, deuterium, tritium). Avogadro's number = . .

    Periodic table: Mendeleev's 1869 table ordered by atomic mass (left gaps for undiscovered elements — he predicted germanium as eka-silicon). Modern table ordered by atomic number (Moseley). Groups are vertical columns (18), periods horizontal (7). Most electropositive: francium (or caesium in practice); most electronegative: fluorine. Noble gases (group 18) are inert — helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon, radon. Transition metals show variable valency (iron Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺).

    Acids, bases, salts: pH scale 0–14 (Sørensen); pure water pH 7; acids < 7 (HCl, H₂SO₄, HNO₃ mineral acids; citric in lemon, acetic in vinegar, lactic in curd, oxalic in tomato), bases > 7 (NaOH caustic soda, Ca(OH)₂ slaked lime, NH₄OH). Neutralisation: acid + base → salt + water. Washing soda = Na₂CO₃·10H₂O; baking soda = NaHCO₃; bleaching powder = CaOCl₂; plaster of Paris = CaSO₄·½H₂O (sets by absorbing water → gypsum CaSO₄·2H₂O); lime water = Ca(OH)₂ solution, turns milky with CO₂.

    Metals & non-metals: most abundant metal in Earth's crust = aluminium; most abundant element overall = oxygen. Metals are malleable/ductile/conductors; best conductor = silver; mercury is liquid at room temperature. Rusting = Fe₂O₃·xH₂O (needs oxygen + water); galvanisation coats iron with zinc. Thermite reaction (Al + Fe₂O₃) welds rails. Stainless steel = Fe + Cr + Ni. Brass = Cu + Zn; bronze = Cu + Sn; solder = Pb + Sn; German silver = Cu + Zn + Ni (no silver — trap).

    Carbon & organic basics: Catenation gives millions of organic compounds. Diamond (hardest natural substance, tetrahedral sp³), graphite (soft, conductor, hexagonal layers — used in pencils and as lubricant), fullerene (C60 buckyball), graphene. Hydrocarbons: alkanes (single bonds, CnH2n+2), alkenes (double), alkynes (triple). Common compounds: methane (CH₄, marsh gas, biogas main component), ethanol (C₂H₅OH, drinking alcohol — denatured with methanol to make it poisonous), vinegar = dilute acetic acid (CH₃COOH), formalin = formaldehyde solution (preservative), chloroform (CHCl₃, anaesthetic), DDT (banned pesticide). Soaps = sodium salts of fatty acids (saponification); detergents clean in hard water (soaps form scum with Ca/Mg).

    Everyday chemistry: LPG = propane + butane; CNG = compressed methane; biogas ≈ 60% methane. Dry ice = solid CO₂. Photographic film uses silver bromide (AgBr). Blue vitriol = CuSO₄·5H₂O. Laughing gas = N₂O. Ozone depletion by CFCs; Montreal Protocol 1987.

    Biology — the living core

    Cell: discovered by Robert Hooke (1665) in cork; cell theory by Schleiden & Schwann. Powerhouse = mitochondria (ATP); kitchen = chloroplast (photosynthesis: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂); control = nucleus (DNA). Cell wall = cellulose (plants); lysosomes = suicide bags; ribosomes = protein synthesis (70S in bacteria, 80S in eukaryotes — antibiotics target 70S).

    Human body systems: Normal body temperature 37°C (98.6°F). Blood: RBCs carry O₂ via haemoglobin (iron-containing; life ~120 days; made in bone marrow), WBCs fight infection (leukocytes), platelets clot. Blood groups: ABO discovered by Karl Landsteiner; O = universal donor, AB = universal recipient; Rh factor (+/−). Normal BP ≈ 120/80 mmHg; pulse ≈ 72/min. Heart: 4 chambers; pacemaker = SA node; largest artery = aorta. Respiration: breathing rate ~16–20/min; alveoli are gas-exchange sites. Digestion: starts in mouth (salivary amylase on starch); stomach HCl + pepsin; liver makes bile (emulsifies fats, stored in gall bladder); pancreas (insulin + glucagon; also digestive enzymes); absorption in small intestine (villi). Excretion: kidneys filter via nephrons. Nervous system: cerebrum (thinking), cerebellum (balance), medulla (breathing/heartbeat); reflex arc via spinal cord. Endocrine glands (ductless): pituitary (master gland), thyroid (thyroxine — iodine needed; deficiency → goitre), adrenal (adrenaline), pancreas, testes/ovaries. Vitamin table — A (retinol: night blindness), D (rickets, sunlight), E (tocopherol), K (clotting), B1 (beriberi), B2 (cheilosis), B3 (pellagra), B12 (pernicious anaemia), C (scurvy). Deficiency diseases are perennial one-mark questions.

    Plant biology: Xylem transports water upward; phloem transports food both ways. Transpiration via stomata; photosynthesis in chloroplasts. Nitrogen fixation by Rhizobium in legume root nodules (pulses — relevant to Bihar's pulse crops).

    Diseases & immunity: Bacterial — TB (Mycobacterium tuberculosis, BCG vaccine), typhoid (Salmonella typhi, Widal test), cholera (Vibrio cholerae), tetanus, diphtheria, plague (rat flea). Viral — smallpox (eradicated 1980; Jenner pioneered vaccination 1796), polio (Sabin/Salk; India certified polio-free 2014), rabies (Pasteur), AIDS (HIV, attacks T-helper cells), dengue/chikungunya (Aedes mosquito), malaria (protozoan Plasmodium, female Anopheles vector — quinine from cinchona bark). Fungal — ringworm, athlete's foot. Vaccines: BCG, DPT, OPV, MMR, pentavalent. Antibiotics (Fleming's penicillin, 1928) work only on bacteria — not viruses (trap).

    High-yield traps

    • Escape velocity 11.2 km/s; geostationary altitude ~35,800 km.
    • Myopia = concave; hypermetropia = convex.
    • Most abundant metal in crust = aluminium, not iron.
    • Plaster of Paris = CaSO₄·½H₂O; gypsum = CaSO₄·2H₂O.
    • O = universal donor, AB = universal recipient (plasma donor logic reverses — AB plasma is universal).
    • Malaria is protozoan, spread by mosquito — not a virus.
    • Antibiotics don't work on viruses.
    • Photosynthesis equation and the roles of xylem vs phloem.

    10. Science & Technology

    ISRO launchers — the ladder to space

    Redraw this from memory — every label is a potential one-mark answer.

    Space — ISRO's ladder

    ISRO founded 1969 (Vikram Sarabhai, father of the Indian space programme); HQ Bengaluru; launch centre Sriharikota (Satish Dhawan Space Centre, SHAR). First satellite Aryabhata (1975), launched by a Soviet rocket. First Indian in space: Rakesh Sharma (1984), aboard Soviet Soyuz T-11 — his famous line to Indira Gandhi: "Saare jahaan se achha." First Indian satellite launch vehicle: SLV-3 (1980, Rohini satellite) under A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.

    Launch vehicles: PSLV (workhorse, polar + sun-synchronous orbits; famous for the 2017 record of 104 satellites in one launch, C37), GSLV Mk II (indigenous cryogenic upper stage — first success 2014), LVM3 / GSLV Mk III (heavy lift, launched Chandrayaan-2 and the LVM3-M3 OneWeb mission). New-gen: SSLV (small satellite, on-demand), and the reusable RLV-TD test vehicle. Human spaceflight: Gaganyaan — India's first crewed mission, targeted after successful uncrewed test flights (TV-D1 abort test passed October 2023; crewed flight targeted ~2026–27, schedule approximate). Astronaut-designates trained in Russia and India.

    Milestone missions: Chandrayaan-1 (2008) — confirmed water molecules on the Moon (with NASA's Moon Mineralogy Mapper); Mangalyaan / Mars Orbiter Mission (2013) — India became the first nation to reach Mars on its first attempt, and the cheapest Mars mission ever (~₹450 crore); Chandrayaan-2 (2019) — orbiter succeeded, Vikram lander crashed; Chandrayaan-3 (2023) — landed near the Moon's south pole (23 August 2023), making India the 4th country to soft-land on the Moon and the first at the south pole; rover Pragyan confirmed sulphur and other elements. Aditya-L1 (2023) — India's first solar observatory, parked at the L1 Lagrange point (~1.5 million km from Earth), studying the solar corona and space weather. XPoSat (Jan 2024) — India's first X-ray polarimetry satellite. SPADEX (Dec 2024) — space docking experiment, a prerequisite for the Bharatiya Antariksh Station (planned ~2035) and future crewed lunar landing (~2040).

    Satellite families: INSAT/GSAT (communication & weather — GSAT), IRS (remote sensing — Cartosat, Resourcesat, RISAT radar imaging), IRNSS/NavIC (India's regional navigation system — 7 satellites, coverage India + 1,500 km; NavIC now recognised by IMO and integrated into some smartphones), EDUSAT/G-SAT education, Astrosat (2015) — India's first dedicated astronomy observatory. GAGAN (GPS-aided geo-augmented navigation, with AAI) improves aviation navigation accuracy.

    Defence & strategic technology

    DRDO (1958, HQ New Delhi) develops the missile families under the IGMDP (Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme) launched 1983 under Kalam: Prithvi (short-range ballistic), Agni series (Agni-I to Agni-V; Agni-V is ICBM-class ~5,000+ km, MIRV-tested with Mission Divyastra, March 2024), Akash (surface-to-air), Nag (anti-tank), Trishul (short-range SAM, later shelved). Beyond IGMDP: BrahMos (supersonic cruise missile, Indo-Russian joint venture, ~Mach 2.8–3; extended range ~450 km+ after MTCR entry in 2016; air-launched from Su-30MKI), Astra (indigenous beyond-visual-range air-to-air), Pinaka (multi-barrel rocket launcher), Dhanush (naval Prithvi variant). S-400 Triumf air defence system procured from Russia (deliveries began 2021). Fighter jets: Tejas (HAL, Light Combat Aircraft, indigenous 4.5-gen), Rafale (French, 36 inducted), AMCA (5th-gen under development). Arihant-class nuclear ballistic submarines (INS Arihant commissioned 2016; INS Arighaat 2024) complete India's nuclear triad. India conducted Mission Shakti (March 2019) — ASAT (anti-satellite) test, 4th country after US, Russia, China.

    Nuclear programme: Homi Bhabha — father of the Indian nuclear programme; AEC (1948), BARC (1957, Trombay). Three-stage programme (Bhabha's plan): PHWR → fast breeder → thorium-based (India holds ~25% of world thorium reserves, in monazite sands of Kerala/Tamil Nadu). Tests: Smiling Buddha (Pokhran-I, 18 May 1974); Pokhran-II (11 & 13 May 1998, Operation Shakti). Nuclear Power Corporation (NPCIL) runs plants: Tarapur (first, 1969), Rawatbhata, Kalpakkam, Narora, Kakrapar, Kaiga, Kudankulam (Russian VVER). INS Arihant's reactor is a naval pressurised-water reactor.

    Biotech, health & digital

    India's COVID-19 vaccines: Covishield (Serum Institute, Oxford-AstraZeneca viral vector) and Covaxin (Bharat Biotech–ICMR, inactivated virus) — the backbone of the world's largest vaccination drive; CoWIN platform managed scheduling; e-RUPI digital vouchers. Genome India Project sequenced 10,000 Indian genomes (2024) for precision medicine. DBT (Department of Biotechnology) runs BIRAC; ICMR (1911, New Delhi) is the apex medical research body. Stem cells: embryonic vs adult; CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing (Nobel 2020, Charpentier & Doudna).

    Digital India stack: Aadhaar (UIDAI, 2009) — world's largest biometric ID; UPI (NPCI, 2016) — India leads the world in real-time digital payments; Jan Dhan–Aadhaar–Mobile (JAM) trinity; ONDC (Open Network for Digital Commerce) for e-commerce democratisation; DigiLocker; UMANG app. 5G rollout began October 2022; India is developing indigenous 6G vision. Semiconductor mission: India Semiconductor Mission with fabs planned (e.g., Dholera, Tata–PSMC). Quantum: National Quantum Mission (2023). AI: IndiaAI Mission (2024) with compute capacity and foundation-model support.

    Energy & frontier science

    Renewable targets: 500 GW non-fossil capacity by 2030 (Panchamrit pledges, COP26 Glasgow 2021; net-zero by 2070). International Solar Alliance (ISA) — launched by India & France at COP21 Paris 2015, HQ Gurugram. National Green Hydrogen Mission (2023). Largest solar parks: Bhadla (Rajasthan) among the world's largest; Pavagada (Karnataka). Nuclear fusion: India's SST-1 tokamak at Gandhinagar; India is a member of the ITER project (France). LIGO-India gravitational-wave detector under construction in Maharashtra (Hingoli). Thirty Meter Telescope — India is a partner. Supercomputers: PARAM series (C-DAC); National Supercomputing Mission; AIRAWAT AI supercomputer (ranked among world's top AI systems).

    High-yield traps

    • Chandrayaan-3 = south pole landing (23 Aug 2023); Chandrayaan-2's lander crashed, orbiter worked.
    • Aditya-L1 sits at the L1 Lagrange point — not orbiting the Moon.
    • NavIC is regional (India + 1,500 km), unlike GPS's global coverage.
    • BrahMos is supersonic (~Mach 3), Indo-Russian; Agni-V is ballistic with MIRV (Mission Divyastra 2024).
    • Pokhran-I 1974 (Smiling Buddha); Pokhran-II 1998.
    • Thorium reserves in monazite sands; three-stage nuclear programme = Bhabha's plan.
    • 5G launched Oct 2022; UPI by NPCI; Aadhaar by UIDAI.

    11. Environment & Ecology

    India’s biodiversity hotspots — four

    Redraw this from memory — every label is a potential one-mark answer.

    Foundations: ecosystem structure

    Ecology (term coined by Ernst Haeckel, 1866) studies organism–environment interactions; ecosystem (term by A.G. Tansley, 1935) = biotic community + abiotic environment. Components: producers (autotrophs — green plants), consumers (primary/herbivores, secondary/carnivores, tertiary), decomposers (bacteria, fungi). Food chain vs food web (interlinked chains); trophic levels; the 10% law (Lindeman) — only ~10% of energy transfers to the next level, the rest lost as heat (why food chains rarely exceed 4–5 levels). Ecological pyramids: number, biomass, energy — the energy pyramid is always upright (trap: biomass/number pyramids can invert in aquatic systems). Ecological succession: primary (bare rock — lichens as pioneers) → secondary (disturbed area) → climax community. Ecotone = transition zone between two ecosystems (high biodiversity — edge effect); ecotype = genetically adapted population; biome = large regional ecosystem (tundra, taiga, grassland, desert, rainforest).

    Biodiversity: levels, hotspots, India

    Three levels: genetic, species, ecosystem diversity. India is one of 17 megadiverse countries, holding ~7–8% of recorded species on ~2.4% of land. Biodiversity hotspots (Norman Myers): 36 globally; 4 in India — Western Ghats & Sri Lanka, Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Sundaland (Nicobar Islands). Endemism is high in the Western Ghats. Red Data Book (IUCN) categories: Extinct, Critically Endangered, Endangered, Vulnerable, Near Threatened, Least Concern. India's threatened icons: Bengal tiger (Endangered), Asiatic lion (only in Gir, Gujarat — Endangered), one-horned rhinoceros (Kaziranga, Assam — Vulnerable), snow leopard, great Indian bustard (Critically Endangered, Rajasthan/Gujarat), Ganges river dolphin (Endangered — India's National Aquatic Animal, found in the Ganga through Bihar), gharial (Critically Endangered, Chambal/Gandak).

    Conservation in India: laws, projects, protected areas

    Constitutional hooks: Article 48A (Directive Principle — state shall protect environment) and Article 51A(g) (fundamental duty of citizens) — both inserted by the 42nd Amendment (1976) (trap: they came together). Laws: Wildlife Protection Act 1972 (schedules I–VI; Schedule I = highest protection, e.g., tiger; amended 2022 to align with CITES), Forest Conservation Act 1980 (amended 2023), Environment Protection Act 1986 (umbrella act after Bhopal), Biological Diversity Act 2002 (Nagoya Protocol; National Biodiversity Authority at Chennai), Forest Rights Act 2006 (rights of forest-dwelling STs and traditional dwellers), Wetlands Rules 2017, EIA Notification 2006. National Green Tribunal (NGT) established 2010.

    Flagship programmes: Project Tiger (1973) — from Jim Corbett; India now has 50+ tiger reserves (2023 count: 54; treat latest additions as approximate) and holds ~75% of the world's wild tigers; Project Elephant (1992); Project Snow Leopard; Cheetah reintroduction — Kuno National Park, Madhya Pradesh (Sept 2022), cheetahs from Namibia/South Africa (first intercontinental translocation of a large carnivore); Project Dolphin (2020) for river and marine dolphins; NAMASTE / Ganga: Namami Gange (2014) under the National Mission for Clean Ganga; Swachh Bharat (2014); Green India Mission (one of 8 National Missions under NAPCC); National Action Plan on Climate Change (2008) with 8 missions. Valmiki Tiger Reserve (West Champaran) is Bihar's only tiger reserve and only national park. Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary (Bhagalpur) — India's only dolphin sanctuary, on the Ganga.

    Protected-area ladder: National Park (strictest — no grazing/habitation; e.g., Valmiki) > Wildlife Sanctuary (some regulated activity; Bihar has ~12, including Gautam Buddha, Kaimur, Rajgir) > Community/Conservation Reserves > Biosphere Reserves (UNESCO MAB programme; 18 in India — Nilgiri was first, 1986; zoned core/buffer/transition). Ramsar sites (wetlands of international importance): India has 80+ (2024–25 additions — treat exact count as approximate); Bihar's Ramsar sites include Kabar Tal (Begusarai) and Nagi–Nakti bird sanctuaries (Jamui) — favourite BPSC options. Eco-Sensitive Zones (ESZ) buffer protected areas (Supreme Court's 1-km default guideline, 2022).

    Pollution, climate, conventions

    Air: major pollutants — PM2.5/PM10, SO₂, NOx, CO, ground-level ozone; AQI scale (Good to Severe+); stubble burning, vehicular emissions, construction dust drive north-India smog. BS-VI emission norms (2020). Water: BOD (biochemical oxygen demand — higher BOD = more polluted), COD, eutrophication (nutrient enrichment → algal blooms → dead zones). Soil: pesticides/fertiliser runoff; biomagnification (DDT concentrating up food chains — classic in fish-eating birds). Noise: measured in dB; safe limit ~55 dB day residential. Minamata Convention (mercury), Stockholm Convention (POPs), Basel Convention (hazardous waste), Rotterdam Convention (PIC procedure). Ozone: Montreal Protocol (1987) — CFC phase-out (Kigali Amendment 2016 adds HFCs); Vienna Convention (1985). Climate: UNFCCC (1992, Rio Earth Summit); Kyoto Protocol (1997) — binding targets for developed nations, CDM mechanism; Paris Agreement (2015, COP21) — NDCs, well-below-2°C goal; India's Panchamrit (net-zero 2070, 500 GW non-fossil by 2030); COP28 Dubai (2023) — first Global Stocktake; COP29 Baku (2024) — new climate finance goal. Carbon concepts: carbon footprint, carbon credits (1 credit = 1 tonne CO₂e), Green Credit Programme (India, 2023), Ecomark rules 2024.

    High-yield traps

    • Energy pyramid always upright; number/biomass can invert.
    • 4 biodiversity hotspots touch India (Western Ghats, Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Sundaland).
    • Art 48A + 51A(g) both came via the 42nd Amendment, 1976.
    • Project Tiger 1973; Project Elephant 1992; Namami Gange 2014.
    • National Aquatic Animal = Ganges river dolphin (not the fish!).
    • Bihar: Valmiki (only NP/tiger reserve), Vikramshila dolphin sanctuary, Kabar Tal Ramsar.
    • Montreal Protocol = ozone/CFCs; Kyoto = binding (developed); Paris = NDCs (all parties).
    • BOD rises with pollution; Minamata = mercury; Stockholm = POPs.

    11.x Bihar's environment — floods, dolphins and wetlands

    Bihar is India's most flood-prone state: roughly three-quarters of north Bihar lies in the flood hazard zone of the Himalayan rivers. The Kosi — the "Sorrow of Bihar" — is infamous for sudden course-shifts; the 2008 Kusaha breach in Nepal displaced over 30 lakh people in Bihar and forced a national rethink of embankment policy. The Kosi Barrage at Bhimnagar, built under the 1954 India–Nepal Kosi agreement, and the vast embankment network remain the backbone of flood control, even as experts debate "living with floods" versus structural control. The Gandak, Bagmati, Burhi Gandak and Mahananda add to the annual monsoon emergency, while south Bihar's rivers (Son, Punpun, Phalgu) swing between flood and drought.

    Bihar's conservation jewels are riverine. The Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary (1991) — a 60-km Ganga stretch at Bhagalpur — is India's only protected area dedicated to the Gangetic dolphin, the National Aquatic Animal, listed as Endangered on the IUCN Red List and in Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act. Project Dolphin (2020) now covers both riverine and marine dolphins on the Project Tiger model. The Valmiki Tiger Reserve in West Champaran — Bihar's only national park — anchors the Terai Arc landscape with Nepal's Chitwan across the border.

    Bihar's wetlands earned global recognition when Kabar Tal (Begusarai) — the state's largest freshwater oxbow lake — became a Ramsar site in 2020, followed by the Nagi and Nakti bird sanctuaries (Jamui). These wetlands sit on the Central Asian Flyway and face the classic threats: eutrophication from fertiliser runoff, encroachment and siltation. Two quieter crises deserve attention: groundwater arsenic in the Gangetic districts (Bhojpur, Buxar, Patna, Bhagalpur belt), and Patna's winter air-quality episodes, which repeatedly place the capital among India's most polluted cities.

    11.y India's climate and conservation ledger, 2024–26

    India's climate commitments rest on the Panchamrit pledges of COP26 (Glasgow, 2021): 500 GW of non-fossil electricity capacity by 2030, 50% of energy from renewables, 1 billion tonnes of emission reduction, 45% emission-intensity cut, and net zero by 2070. At COP29 (Baku, 2024), developed nations agreed to a $300 billion-per-year climate finance goal — which India criticised as too little, too late — sharpening the equity debate BPSC mains answers must reflect.

    Domestically, the green-economy architecture thickened: the National Green Hydrogen Mission (approved January 2023, outlay Rs 19,744 crore) targets 5 million metric tonnes of annual green-hydrogen production by 2030; the Green Credit Programme (2023) rewards voluntary environmental action; Ecomark rules (2024) certify genuinely green products; and Mission LiFE promotes lifestyle-level change. For Bihar specifically, PM-KUSUM (2019) — the central scheme for solarising agricultural feeders and pumps — is the policy vehicle behind the state's solar-irrigation push, directly linking the energy and agriculture syllabi.

    High-yield linkages for revision: Kosi 1954 agreement = India–Nepal water diplomacy · Vikramshila 1991 = only dolphin sanctuary · Kabar Tal 2020 = Ramsar · Project Dolphin 2020 = on Project Tiger lines · Green Hydrogen Mission (2023) = Rs 19,744 crore outlay · net zero 2070 = Panchamrit · COP29 Baku = $300 billion finance goal.

    12. Bihar GK (Districts, Rivers, Folk Arts, Festivals)

    State profile at a glance

    Bihar: formed 22 March 1912 (Bihar Day) as a separate province from Bengal Presidency; became a state on 26 January 1950; Jharkhand carved out on 15 November 2000 — Bihar went from India's largest mineral state to an agrarian one overnight (a favourite "cause–effect" mains point). Capital Patna (ancient Pataliputra). Area ~94,163 sq km; 38 districts, 9 divisions; official languages Hindi and Urdu. State symbols: tree — peepal; flower — marigold (genda); animal — ox (bail); bird — sparrow (gauraiya). Population (2011 Census): ~10.41 crore — 3rd most populous state (after UP and Maharashtra); density ~1,106/sq km — highest among major states; sex ratio 918 (national 943); literacy 61.8% (lowest among major states in 2011; female literacy 51.5%). Per the 2022–23 Bihar caste-based survey: EBCs ~36%, OBCs ~27%, SCs ~19.65%, STs ~1.68%, General ~15.5% (figures approximate — released October 2023).

    Ancient history — Bihar's golden chapters

    Bihar is the cradle of two world religions and India's first empires. Magadha (capital Rajagriha, later Pataliputra) rose under Bimbisara (founder of the Haryanka dynasty) and Ajatshatru (fortified Pataliputra). Mahavira (born Kundagrama, Vaishali ~540 BCE) founded Jainism's final form; Buddha attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya (~531 BCE) and preached his first sermon at Sarnath (UP). The first Buddhist council was at Rajagriha (Rajgir); the third at Pataliputra under Ashoka. Chandragupta Maurya (with Chanakya/Kautilya, author of the Arthashastra) founded the Mauryan Empire ~321 BCE; Ashoka (r. ~268–232 BCE) embraced Buddhism after the Kalinga War (261 BCE) and spread Dhamma via edicts (his pillars at Lauriya Nandangarh, Rampurva, Kolhua-Vaishali are in Bihar). The Nalanda Mahavihara (founded by Kumaragupta I, Gupta era, 5th century CE) was the world's first residential university — destroyed by Bakhtiyar Khilji ~1193 CE; Vikramshila (founded by Dharmapala, Pala dynasty) met a similar fate. UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Bihar: Mahabodhi Temple, Bodh Gaya (2002) and Nalanda Mahavihara ruins (2016).

    Medieval–modern: Sher Shah Suri (born Sasaram, Bihar) — built the Grand Trunk Road (Sadak-e-Azam), introduced the rupiya currency and land-revenue reforms; his tomb is at Sasaram. Guru Gobind Singh (10th Sikh Guru) was born at Patna Sahib (1666) — Takht Sri Harmandir Sahib. 1857: Veer Kunwar Singh (Jagdispur, Bhojpur), aged ~80, led the revolt in Bihar — victories at Arrah (defeated Captain Dunbar). Champaran Satyagraha (1917) — Gandhi's first satyagraha in India, against the tinkathia system forcing indigo cultivation (Rajkumar Shukla invited him). Jayaprakash Narayan (born Sitab Diara, Saran) led the Total Revolution (Sampoorna Kranti, 1974) and the anti-Emergency movement; Dr Rajendra Prasad (born Zeradei, Siwan) — first President of India.

    Districts & divisions — the 38

    Nine divisions: Patna, Tirhut (Muzaffarpur), Saran (Chhapra), Darbhanga, Kosi (Saharsa), Purnia, Bhagalpur, Munger, Magadh (Gaya). Memorise by region: North Bihar (north of the Ganga — Tirhut, Saran, Darbhanga, Kosi, Purnia divisions: e.g., West/East Champaran, Muzaffarpur, Sitamarhi, Sheohar, Darbhanga, Madhubani, Samastipur, Saharsa, Supaul, Madhepura, Purnia, Katihar, Araria, Kishanganj); South Bihar (Patna, Magadh, Bhagalpur, Munger divisions: Patna, Nalanda, Bhojpur, Buxar, Rohtas, Kaimur, Gaya, Jehanabad, Arwal, Nawada, Aurangabad, Bhagalpur, Banka, Munger, Jamui, Lakhisarai, Sheikhpura, Khagaria). Traps: Kishanganj is Bihar's only Muslim-majority district and touches West Bengal; West Champaran borders Nepal and UP; Kaimur borders UP; Arwal is the smallest district (newest, carved 2001); Jamui is heavily forested. The Ganga divides Bihar into North and South — most "which side" questions key off this.

    Bihar's administrative ladder — Division to Panchayat

    Redraw this from memory — every label is a potential one-mark answer.

    Rivers — the lifeline map

    The Ganga enters Bihar at Chausa (Buxar) and exits near Bhagalpur, flowing ~445 km through the state. North-bank tributaries (Himalayan, flood-prone): Ghaghra/Sarayu (joins at Chhapra/Revelganj), Gandak (joins at Hajipur/Sonepur — note: Sonepur's Harihar Kshetra Mela sits at the Gandak–Ganga confluence), Budhi Gandak, Bagmati, Kamla, Kosi ("Sorrow of Bihar" — joins at Kursela, Katihar; infamous for shifting course; Kosi Barrage at Bhimnagar), Mahananda. South-bank tributaries: Sone (joins at Maner, west of Patna — second-largest Ganga tributary after Yamuna), Punpun (joins at Fatuha), Kiull–Harohar, Falgu (flows by Gaya — the Pitrapaksha rites at Vishnupad use its banks; it flows underground at Gaya), Chandan/Ajay. Sone originates at Amarkantak (same source as the Narmada). Floods: North Bihar's Kosi–Gandak–Bagmati belt is India's most flood-prone; South Bihar faces drought in the plateau fringe (Kaimur). Trap: Kosi joins the Ganga in Bihar (Kursela), not in Nepal; the Gandak forms part of the UP–Bihar border.

    Folk arts, crafts & festivals

    Madhubani/Mithila painting — GI-tagged, from the Mithila region (Madhubani district); styles: Bharni, Katchni, Tantrik, Godna; traditionally done with fingers, twigs, and natural dyes on walls/paper; artists like Sita Devi, Ganga Devi, Mahasundari Devi. Other crafts: Sujini embroidery (Bhusra, Muzaffarpur), sikki grass work, lac bangles, Bhagalpuri silk (tussar), stone carving of Gaya/Pattharkatti. Folk dances: Jhijhiya (Mithila, women's dance balancing pots), Jat-Jatin (North Bihar, man–woman pair), Paika (martial, Munda-influenced), Sama-Chakeva (Mithila, brother–sister theme, winter), Domkach (wedding dance). Folk theatre: Bidesia (Bhikhari Thakur — the "Shakespeare of Bhojpuri"); Nautanki. Music: Bhojpuri, Maithili, Magahi, Angika, Vajjika dialects; singers like Sharda Sinha (Chhath songs).

    Festivals: Chhath (Bihar's signature — Sun god + Chhathi Maiya; Nahay-Khay, Kharna, Sandhya Arghya, Usha Arghya; Kartik month) — the single most asked festival. Sama-Chakeva (Mithila), Madhushravani (Maithil women's festival), Jitiya/Jivitputrika (mothers' fast for children), Teej, Sonepur Mela (Asia's largest cattle fair, Kartik Purnima, at the Gandak–Ganga confluence), Pitrapaksha Mela (Gaya), Rajgir Mahotsav, Buddha Purnima (Bodh Gaya), Malmas Mela. Languages: Maithili is in the 8th Schedule (92nd Amendment, 2003 — with Bodo, Dogri, Santhali); Bhojpuri/Magahi/Angika are demanded but not scheduled (trap).

    Polity & administration quick-hits

    Bihar Legislative Assembly: 243 seats; Legislative Council: 75 seats; Lok Sabha: 40 seats; Rajya Sabha: 16 seats. High Court at Patna (est. 1916). First CM: Shri Krishna Sinha (Sri Babu); first Governor: Jairamdas Daulatram. Panchayati Raj: Bihar was early to 50% reservation for women in panchayats (2006) and urban local bodies. Bihar Public Service Commission HQ at Patna (Bailey Road); constituted under Article 315. Bihar's state animal/bird/tree/flower listed above are direct one-markers.

    High-yield traps

    • Bihar Day = 22 March 1912 (separation from Bengal), not 1950 or 2000.
    • Ganga enters at Chausa (Buxar); Kosi = "Sorrow of Bihar", joins at Kursela.
    • Maithili is 8th Schedule (2003); Bhojpuri is not.
    • Nalanda (2016) and Mahabodhi (2002) are the two UNESCO sites.
    • Champaran 1917 = Gandhi's first satyagraha; tinkathia = indigo.
    • 243 Assembly / 40 Lok Sabha / 16 Rajya Sabha seats.
    • First President (Rajendra Prasad) and JP — both Bihar-born.
    • Falgu flows underground at Gaya; Sone originates at Amarkantak.

    13. Mental Ability & Reasoning

    How BPSC tests this

    Reasoning in BPSC is speed arithmetic plus pattern logic — roughly 10–15 questions. The syllabus-adjacent core: number series, coding-decoding, blood relations, direction sense, syllogisms, seating arrangement, analogies, odd-one-out, statement–conclusion, data interpretation basics, and arithmetic word problems (percentages, ratios, averages, time–speed–distance, time–work, profit–loss, simple/compound interest). Learn the formula, then a 30-second method.

    Number series — the five moves

    When stuck, test in order: (1) constant difference (AP: 3, 7, 11, 15… +4); (2) difference of differences (2, 6, 12, 20, 30… differences 4, 6, 8, 10); (3) multiplication pattern (2, 6, 18, 54… ×3; or ×2+1, ×3−2 mixes); (4) squares/cubes ± n (1, 2, 5, 10, 17… = n²+1; 1, 8, 27, 64… cubes); (5) alternate/interleaved series (1, 5, 2, 10, 3, 15… — odd positions 1, 2, 3; even positions ×5). Also primes (2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13…) and Fibonacci (each term = sum of previous two: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13…). Trap: mixed operations like ×2+3, ×2+4 (2, 7, 18, 39… → ×2+3, ×2+4, ×2+5).

    Coding-decoding — anchor on A=1

    Write A–Z as 1–26 (and reverse Z=1). Common patterns: letter shift (CAT → DBU: +1 each; "forward coding"), reverse shift, opposite letters (A↔Z, B�=Y… sum = 27: A(1)+Z(26)=27), position sum/product (CAT = 3+1+20 = 24), number codes (each letter replaced by a digit per a key). Method: always compute the shift for the first two letters before assuming; check whether the pattern applies to vowels only or consonants only in harder variants. Example: if MANGO = 13114715, that's just letter positions (M=13, A=1, N=14, G=7, O=15) concatenated.

    Blood relations — draw the tree

    Build a family tree top-down; mark gender with +/−. Key decodings: "A is B's father's brother's son" = A's father is B's father's brother → A and B are cousins. "Mother's brother" = maternal uncle; "father's sister" = paternal aunt; "sister's husband" = brother-in-law. Pointing puzzles ("pointing to a photo, X said 'she is the daughter of my grandfather's only son'") — grandfather's only son = father → "father's daughter" = sister (or X herself if female — read options). Always resolve "only son/only daughter" first; that's the hinge.

    Directions — fix north first

    Standard: North up, East right. Right turn from North faces East; left turn faces West. Track net displacement with a rough sketch, not memory. Common twist: "walks 5 km north, turns right, walks 3 km" → ends 3 km east of start; distance from start = √(5²+3²) = √34 km (Pythagoras). Shadow logic: at sunrise shadows fall west; at sunset, east — used in "X's shadow fell to his right, which way was he facing?" (morning + shadow right = facing south… work it: morning sun in east, shadow west; if shadow is on his right, west is right → facing north? Careful: facing south, right hand = west. So shadow west on right = facing south.)

    Syllogisms — Venn it

    Draw overlapping circles; the conclusion must hold in every valid diagram. Rules that kill most errors: (1) "All A are B" does not imply "All B are A" (converse error — the classic trap); (2) from two negative premises ("No A is B", "No B is C") nothing follows; (3) a particular conclusion needs a particular premise; (4) "Some A are B" converts to "Some B are A" — valid. Statement–conclusion vs statement–assumption: conclusions must be directly derivable; assumptions are unstated but necessary for the statement to make sense.

    Seating & puzzles — anchor one person

    Circular arrangement: fix one person's seat, place others relative to them; "facing the centre" means left/right are mirrored vs facing outward (draw arrows). Linear: mark ends, fill definite positions first, keep possibilities as branches — never guess a branch, carry both. Blood-relation + seating hybrids: solve relations first. Floor puzzles: number floors bottom-up unless stated.

    Arithmetic word problems — the formula sheet

    Percentages: x% of y = (x/100)×y; percentage change = (change/original)×100. Ratio–proportion: a:b = c:d → ad = bc; divide ₹X in ratio m:n → shares Xm/(m+n), Xn/(m+n). Average: sum/n; average speed for equal distances = 2xy/(x+y) (harmonic mean — trap: not (x+y)/2). Time–work: A does 1/a per day, B 1/b → together 1/a+1/b; work = rate × time; "A is twice as efficient as B" → A takes half the time. Time–speed–distance: d = s×t; km/h → m/s multiply by 5/18; trains: crossing a pole = length/speed; crossing each other (opposite) = (L1+L2)/(s1+s2). Profit–loss: profit% = (profit/CP)×100 — always on cost price (trap: computing on SP); SP = CP×(1+p/100). Simple interest: SI = PRT/100; compound: A = P(1+r/100)ⁿ. Mixtures: alligation — (cheaper qty):(dearer qty) = (dearer price − mean):(mean − cheaper price).

    Data interpretation — read before computing

    Scan the question stem first, then the table/graph — compute only what's asked. Bar/line/pie basics: pie angle = (value/total)×360°. Growth rate = (new−old)/old. In tables, watch units (₹ crore vs ₹ lakh; '000s) — unit mismatch is the designed trap. Approximate aggressively: 47.8 ≈ 48 when options are far apart.

    High-yield traps

    • Average speed over equal distances = 2xy/(x+y), not the simple mean.
    • Profit% is on cost price, never on selling price.
    • "All A are B" ⇏ "All B are A" — the converse error.
    • Opposite letters sum to 27 (A+Z, B+Y…). Anchor A=1, Z=26.
    • Circular seating facing centre: left/right are mirrored.
    • km/h → m/s: multiply by 5/18.
    • In DI, check units before calculating.

    14. Current Affairs 2025–26 (Bihar + National)

    How to use this chapter: current-affairs questions in BPSC reward the why behind the headline — the institution, the constitutional hook, or the Bihar angle. Dates and designations below reflect the position as of September 2026; treat fast-moving numbers (counts, rankings) as approximate and cross-check with a current newspaper before the exam.

    National polity & governance

    General Elections 2024 returned the BJP-led NDA for a third term with Narendra Modi as Prime Minister (sworn in 9 June 2024); the Lok Sabha has a stronger opposition than 2014/2019, with Rahul Gandhi as Leader of the Opposition. One Nation One Election: the Kovind Committee report (2024) recommended simultaneous polls; the Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha in December 2024 and referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee — a live mains topic (federalism, Article 83/172 tenure questions). The Women's Reservation Act (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023 — 106th Amendment) reserves one-third of seats in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies, effective after the next delimitation following the census.

    Census: the long-delayed Census 2027 was announced with caste enumeration included — the first caste census since 1931 (the 2011 SECC data was never fully released). Delimitation of Lok Sabha seats follows. New criminal laws replaced the colonial codes from 1 July 2024: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (IPC), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (CrPC), Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (Evidence Act). The Waqf (Amendment) Act 2025 (passed April 2025) restructured waqf administration — expect questions on its key provisions (collector's role in disputed properties, non-Muslim members on boards). DPDP Act 2023 (Digital Personal Data Protection) — India's first data-privacy law; rules notified in phases.

    Economy & budgets 2025–26

    Union Budget 2025–26 (presented 1 February 2025 by Nirmala Sitharaman): headline — income tax relief with no tax up to ₹12 lakh under the new regime (₹12.75 lakh for salaried with standard deduction); fiscal deficit targeted ~4.4% of GDP. Bihar Budget 2025–26 was presented in the assembly in March 2025 (size ~₹3.17 lakh crore — approximate); the 2026–27 budget followed in February 2026 — keep year-specific figures approximate and verify near the exam. GST reforms (2025): the GST Council approved a major rate rationalisation to essentially two slabs (5% and 18%) with a 40% demerit rate, effective September 2025 — a landmark prelims fact (101st Amendment background, Article 279A council). RBI: Sanjay Malhotra took over as Governor in December 2024; the MPC cut the repo rate through 2025 as inflation cooled (exact rate moves are time-sensitive — verify). UPI continued record transaction volumes; the Digital Rupee (e₹) pilots expanded.

    Science, space & defence milestones

    Chandrayaan-3's south-pole landing (August 2023) remained the reference achievement; Aditya-L1 began full solar observations from the L1 point; Gaganyaan progressed through uncrewed abort tests (TV-D1, 2023) toward a crewed flight targeted in the 2026–27 window (schedule approximate). SPADEX docking experiment (December 2024) succeeded — a step toward the Bharatiya Antariksh Station (~2035). Defence: Mission Divyastra (March 2024) tested MIRV technology on Agni-V; INS Arighaat (second Arihant-class SSBN) commissioned August 2024; Tejas Mk1A deliveries and AMCA 5th-gen fighter development continued; the S-400 squadrons were operationalised. India–France Rafale-Marine deal (2025) for 26 carrier-based jets was signed (approximate status — verify).

    Environment & climate

    COP29 (Baku, 2024) agreed a new climate-finance goal (~$300 billion/year by 2035 — developing nations called it inadequate); COP30 was scheduled in Belém, Brazil (November 2025). India pushed the International Solar Alliance and Green Hydrogen Mission; Mission LiFE remained the behavioural-climate flagship. Project Cheetah at Kuno saw cubs born in the wild (2023–24) alongside mortality setbacks — a balanced prelims/mains point on reintroduction science. Tiger census figures (~3,682 in the 2022 estimate; next all-India estimation cycle due) — verify latest. Ramsar sites in India crossed 80+ with 2024–25 additions. In Bihar: Kabar Tal and Nagi–Nakti Ramsar status; Vikramshila Dolphin Sanctuary work under Project Dolphin; recurring Kosi–Gandak floods and Patna's air-quality episodes stayed in the news.

    Bihar-specific current affairs

    Bihar Assembly Elections 2025 (held October–November 2025): the NDA returned to power and Nitish Kumar continued as Chief Minister — verify seat tallies and alliance details near the exam, as post-poll alignments move. The caste-based survey (2023) continued shaping reservation politics: Bihar raised quotas via 2023 legislation (65% total), which the Patna High Court struck down in June 2024 for breaching the 50% ceiling (Indra Sawhney) — a landmark polity question. The state then sought 9th Schedule protection — classic mains material (judicial review vs parliamentary supremacy).

    Development news: Patna Metro construction advanced toward phased opening (verify operational status); the New Nalanda University campus (inaugurated June 2024) began full academic operations; AIIMS Darbhanga construction progressed; the Munger–Bhagalpur rail/road bridge projects and JP Ganga Path (Patna Marine Drive) extensions continued. Makhana got a national push — the Union Budget 2025–26 announced a Makhana Board in Bihar (a direct Bihar-economy prelims fact). Bihar's GI tags expanded (Mithila makhana, Bhagalpuri silk, Sikki grass work, Sujini embroidery — verify the latest list). BPSC's 70th CCE prelims (December 2024) faced paper-leak protests and a re-exam at one Patna centre — the 70th BPSC mains and 71st CCE cycle followed through 2025–26 (verify current cycle status at bpsc.bihar.gov.in).

    Sports & awards

    Paris Olympics 2024: India won 6 medals (1 silver — Neeraj Chopra, javelin; 5 bronze — including Manu Bhaker's two shooting bronzes, Swapnil Kusale, Aman Sehrawat, and the men's hockey team). Paralympics 2024: India won a record 29 medals. Chess: D. Gukesh became the World Chess Champion (December 2024) — youngest ever at 18, defeating Ding Liren; India also won both golds at the 2024 Chess Olympiad. Cricket: India won the 2024 T20 World Cup (June 2024, Barbados) and the 2025 Champions Trophy (March 2025, Dubai). Awards: Bharat Ratna 2024 — Karpoori Thakur (Bihar's own, posthumous), L.K. Advani, P.V. Narasimha Rao (posthumous), Charan Singh (posthumous), M.S. Swaminathan (posthumous). Nobel Prizes 2024/2025: verify laureates near the exam (2024 — Physics: Hopfield & Hinton for machine learning; Chemistry: Baker, Hassabis & Jumper for protein structure; Peace: Nihon Hidankyo).

    International snapshot

    US elections 2024: Donald Trump returned as President (inaugurated January 2025); US tariff moves in 2025 affected Indian exports — a live economy/IR topic. India–US: defence and technology cooperation (iCET) continued; India–Russia energy and S-400 ties persisted amid the Ukraine war; India–China: the October 2024 border-patrol agreement eased the Ladakh standoff, with phased disengagement. G20: Brazil hosted 2024 (Rio), South Africa 2025 (Johannesburg). BRICS expanded with new members (2024–25 additions — verify the current list). UN: India's push for Security Council reform continued.

    High-yield traps

    • Women's reservation = 106th Amendment (2023), effective only after delimitation post-census.
    • New criminal laws effective 1 July 2024: BNS / BNSS / BSA.
    • Census 2027 includes caste enumeration — first since 1931.
    • GST 2025 reform: 5%/18% core slabs + 40% demerit rate.
    • Patna HC struck down Bihar's 65% quota (June 2024) — 50% ceiling (Indra Sawhney).
    • Bharat Ratna 2024 included Karpoori Thakur (Bihar).
    • Gukesh = youngest World Chess Champion (Dec 2024); Paris 2024 = 6 medals; Paralympics = record 29.
    • Verify fast-moving facts (election tallies, metro status, BPSC cycle) at official sources before the exam.

    06 · Mains answer craft

    Make every page easy to reward

    A strong answer is not the longest one. It identifies the demand, gives organised evidence and closes with an administratively useful way forward.

    D
    Decode the directiveDiscuss, analyse, evaluate, examine and comment require different depth.
    S
    Structure before sentencesTake 30–45 seconds: introduction, 3–5 subheads, conclusion.
    E
    Evidence + BiharAdd a constitutional provision, report, example, case or local administrative lens.
    W
    Way forwardEnd with feasible, balanced and rights-respecting recommendations.

    Progressive answer-writing ladder

    1. Weeks 1–2: write only outlines for one PYQ a day.
    2. Weeks 3–4: write three full answers each week without strict timing.
    3. Weeks 5–8: write five timed answers weekly; self-check relevance and structure.
    4. After week 8: one sectional test weekly plus a full essay every fortnight.
    5. Final phase: full-length papers at the actual pace and word limits in your notice.
    Self-check: answered the exact question · balanced dimensions · Bihar link · readable headings · sourced data with year · complete conclusion.
    07 · PYQ method

    Mine papers; do not merely solve them

    Previous papers reveal the commission’s language, depth and recurring zones. Use a four-pass system.

    Pass 1 · Diagnose

    Attempt cold. Mark every answer as know / confused / guessed / unknown. Do not look at solutions mid-paper.

    Pass 2 · Classify

    Tag each question by syllabus topic, Bihar-specificity and source. Repeated tags become priority chapters.

    Pass 3 · Repair

    Write the reason your answer failed: concept gap, fact gap, poor elimination, haste or misreading.

    Pass 4 · Re-test

    Reattempt wrong questions after 7 days and the full paper after 30 days under timed conditions.

    Practice with 3,539 real items

    Quiz complete

    09 · Personality test

    Prepare judgement, not a performance

    Create a one-page dossier for each theme below. Speak in short, reasoned answers; acknowledge trade-offs and facts you do not know.

    Your district

    Economy, history, geography, administration, two problems and workable solutions.

    Your profile

    Graduation, employment gaps, hobbies, achievements and why public service now.

    Bihar today

    Development, education, health, floods, migration, agriculture, cities and social inclusion.

    Why BPSC, and what would public service let you do that your current path would not?
    Choose one persistent problem in your district. What can a subdivisional officer realistically change in one year?
    How would you balance fast relief, due process and limited resources during a flood?
    Name one Bihar policy you support and one improvement you would recommend.
    What would you do if a lawful order is unpopular but necessary?
